input.body:
label: bug
file: src/util/dates.ts

`isRollupDue` decides whether "now" falls within the first day of the user's
week by calling `startOfWeek(now, user.timezone)` and checking that less than
24h have passed since that boundary. But `startOfWeek` in `src/util/dates.ts`
has a `// TODO: honour tz` — it computes the week start purely from
`getUTCDay()`/`setUTCDate()`, ignoring the `tz` parameter entirely.

For a user in London (UTC/UTC+1), the UTC calendar day mostly coincides with
the local day, so the Monday-in-UTC boundary is close enough to the
Monday-in-local-time boundary and the rollup fires correctly. For a user in
Sydney (UTC+10/+11), local Monday begins 10–11 hours before UTC Monday does,
so the computed `weekStart` is effectively anchored to the wrong local day:
by the time `now - weekStart < DAY_MS` and `localHour == 8` both hold for
Sydney, local wall-clock time has already rolled into Tuesday. That's exactly
the "Monday email arrives Tuesday, but only for Sydney" symptom reported.

The fix belongs in `startOfWeek`, which needs to actually compute the start
of the week in the given IANA time zone (e.g. by formatting `d` into local
y/m/d via `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `tz`, finding the local weekday, and
subtracting days in local time) rather than operating on UTC fields.
